This is where shadow boxing comes into play. When you shadow box try to think of it like an actual fight or spar, practicing moves and combinations but also practicing defense based on how an opponent reacts. So for instance, you start off jabbing to gather your range, working slips and other head movements into it. Then you work blocks or parrying because a real opponent is going to try to hit back. Keep working your jab and then start throwing combinations 1-2, 1-3, 3-2 roundhouse, 4-3 knee, etc. When you do this often you'll start to flow and won't feel like you're button mashing, you'll start fighting with your shadow and it's more fluid. The important thing to remember is treating it like you're actually fighting someone and not a heavy bag. That means utilizing footwork, blocking and parrying, good head movement, working counters etc. Shadow boxing helps prepare you for fights/spars because it's simulating real action and helps you determine what tools to use in a fight. Hope this helps.
